The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica Last updated Apr. 12, 2026 Dustin Johnson holds the record for the lowest 72-hole score at the Masters Tournament: 268. He set the record in 2020, shooting 20 under par. The previous record was held by Tiger Woods (1997) and Jordan Spieth (2015), both of whom shot 270. The lowest score after an 18-hole round is 63, set by Nick Price (1986) and Greg Norman (1996). Related Questions What is the Masters Tournament? What does the winner of the Masters Tournament get? The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica Last updated Apr. 12, 2026 The Masters Tournament is an invitational golf tournament held annually since 1934 at the Augusta National Golf Club in Augusta, Georgia. It is played from Thursday through Sunday during the first full week of April. The Masters was conceived by Bobby Jones and is one of the four major golf tournaments, along with the U.S. Open, the British Open (Open Championship), and the PGA Championship. The winner receives a cash prize, a gold medal, a lifetime invitation to the Masters, and invitations to the other three majors for the next five years. Since 1949, winners have also been presented with a distinctive green jacket. Related Questions What does the winner of the Masters Tournament get?
